newsitem.title: FRANCE: France beefs up troops in rebel-hit Central Africa.
newsitem.headline: France beefs up troops in rebel-hit Central Africa.

text.p: France has beefed up its military presence in Bangui, capital of the Central African Republic where a mutiny broke out last weekend among local government troops, the French Defence Ministry said on Thursday.
"The French contingent in the city now numbers about 1,500 men with the arrival of a company of reinforcements from our base at N'Djamena (Chad)," a senior officer told a news briefing.
The reinforcements were drawn from the Foreign Legion's Second Parachute Regiment. Most of the troops already in Bangui are marines.
The officer said the situation in Bangui was calm and there were talks between the government and mutineers on how to defuse the situation.
The mutineers numbered less than 400 and were split in two separate locations, said the French officer, who spoke on condition of anonymity.

The mutineers, who also staged a pay revolt in April, on Saturday revived demands for back pay from 1992 and 1993 and for President Ange-Felix Patasse to revoke a decree ordering one of the regiments involved in revolts to a base out of the capital.
They also seek implementation of recommendations made by a national conference after the May revolt, including forming a professional army with a greater role in national life.
French officials believe the mutineers want to overthrow the government and are in contact with opposition politicians.
France, which has two bases in the Central African Republic, stepped in during the past revolts to prop up the local government which is allied to Paris.
